title: A Mongoose Hunts Cobras Because Venom Barely Touches It

scenes.text: This small animal hunts cobras. The venom should paralyze it.
Cobra venom works by locking onto receptors that carry signals from nerves to muscles.
That shuts the muscles down. In most animals, it means paralysis.
But the mongoose has a changed version of that receptor.
Scientists found a small sugar attached to it that physically blocks the toxin from latching on.
The venom bounces off. The cobra's weapon fails on the one animal that hunts it.

description:
This small animal hunts cobras, and the venom should paralyze it.
Its nerve receptors are altered so the toxin cannot grab on.
Would you have guessed a sugar could block a venom?
first_comment: Cobra or mongoose: who would you bet on? Tell us which animal to cover next.
